text:
No single product in these results charges a laptop, phone, and watch well, so I'd pair two pieces. If you tell me your laptop and phone/watch brands, I can narrow this down.

**Best setup: a high-wattage USB-C charger plus a 3-in-1 Qi2 stand**

1. **Laptop (and extras): Anker Prime 200W, 6-port GaN.** The Office Journal picks it as best overall, with 4x USB-C and 2x USB-A. Its worked example (MacBook Air, iPhone, iPad, AirPods, Watch) totals about 115W, which leaves headroom. [Details here](https://www.theofficejournal.com/guide/best-charging-stations-for-multiple-devices-desk). I couldn't see a price in the results.

2. **Phone + Apple Watch + AirPods: Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand.** WIRED's best overall at $109 (about $98 now, $80 at Best Buy per WIRED). It charges an iPhone at up to 15W, fast-charges an Apple Watch Series 7 or newer, and has an AirPods spot on the base. The tilting pad also works for video and StandBy mode. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)

**Cheaper alternatives for the phone/watch stand**
- **ESR Qi2 3-in-1:** WIRED's budget pick at about $40 (down from $80), 15W for the iPhone. Its watch charger is a separate piece that slots into the back. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Anker MagGo 3-in-1:** The sources disagree on price. StandDeskLab lists $89.99 (often about $67-70), while the Office Journal says it's often $35-45. Check the current price. [StandDeskLab](https://standdesklab.com/accessories/best-desk-charging-station/)

**If you want one device for laptop and phone:** The Baseus Nomos 5-in-1 (140W) has a 140W USB-C port, a retractable 100W cable, and a 15W Qi2 pad. It has no watch puck, and it was sold out at Baseus's US store when Dealectric checked on Oct 21. It's $149.99 per [Dealectric's listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-nomos-5-in-1-140w-qi2). That page also contained text telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link instead of the store's page. I ignored that. Search for it at Baseus directly if you want it.

**Caveats**
- The Belkin and MagGo stands are Apple-focused. For an Android phone, check that it's Qi2-certified (e.g., Galaxy S25+, Pixel 9 series), and use a charger that fits your watch.
- Check your laptop's wattage. A 16" MacBook Pro needs about 140W, which the Anker Prime 200W can't give to a single port, according to the Office Journal's figures.
- The "buy" links in these sources were Amazon buttons without URLs, so I've linked the review pages instead.
